commits.message:
refactor(daemon): a launch carries its owner, so a closed daemon's work is refused (candybar-testing-0x6u.snf) (#523)

* refactor(daemon): a launch carries its owner, so a closed daemon's work is refused (candybar-testing-0x6u.snf)

Launch state lived in module globals, and a closed daemon's scope stayed in
force only until the next daemon replaced it. A closed daemon's unwinding pass
then read the new live scope on its next launch: it ran under the second
daemon, landed in its stats, and was ended by its close. Production never
reaches this, because it builds one daemon per process. A jest worker does on
every restart, and the epic moves every restart onto one.

Launch state is now a value, `createLauncher`, holding the scope, the rate
limits, the launches in flight and the lifeline. `createDaemon` builds one and
its work holds it, so a closed daemon's launches stay refused whichever daemon
is live. There is no ambient `launch`: every call site names its owner, and
eslint keeps the process's launcher, `createLauncher` and `dlog` to their
owners. One daemon is still live in a process, now because its paths and its
log are read from the process's environment.

A refused launch is metered, so one that did nothing reads apart from one
nobody tried. That count is the fact the restart test waits on; a count of
children reads the same either way. A line logged after a close has finished
says so, because that file can be the next daemon's log.

* refactor(daemon): a daemon's storage logs through it, and one gate answers every refusal (candybar-testing-0x6u.snf)

From the high review of this branch.

A write in flight at the close finishes after it, and what it logged had no
stamp, so "a line logged after a close says so" was false for storage. Storage
is built before the daemon, so it could not hold the daemon's log: `storage` is
now a function of that log, and `file-storage.ts` leaves the `dlog` owners.

A launch its own caller had aborted skipped `admit`, so it was unmetered. A job
reported every refusal as the daemon closing, whatever `admit` had said. A
refusal now always carries its reason, and the job passes it through.

The context field was `dlog` but held the stamped log, which is how the "daemon
passes `dlog`" comments went stale, so it is now `log`. Also: the refused rows
count toward the stats column's width, `claimAct` takes its reader rather than
defaulting one for tests, and `__lifelineForTest` moves off `Launcher` onto
what `createLauncher` returns.

* refactor(daemon): a refusal says why in the words of whoever aborted it, and daemon-imported files launch through a launcher they are handed (candybar-testing-0x6u.snf)

From the medium review of this branch.

A refusal's text was one literal, so a closed daemon and a caller's abort read
alike, and a shell source's failure gained a redundant "aborted: aborted before
it started". The text now comes from the signal's own reason: the daemon's close
already says "the daemon closed", and a caller says what it means.

`src/doctor/handler-probe.ts` and `src/install/index.ts` owned `processLauncher`
while daemon code imports them, so a launch added there and reached from a click
would pass lint and escape the close. They now take a launcher, and the owners
list holds `src/index.ts` and the doctor's CLI instead.

`subprocessRefused` is a read-only view, and its comment says what it counts,
which includes a caller's abort. The bench and the draw-reserve reader anchor
on where the event starts, so the rule in testing.md has no exception.

feat(carousel): the standard control names the setting it changes, not its value (brandon-menus-sjhy.vxr)

{{ carousel "apply" "open" "label" }} draws ◀ label ▶. The label is required, the neighbour ring and the themeSwitcher segment are gone, and a value outside the domain counts as the first member.
feat(site): the live bar's font size is a slider
feat(site): the live bar's font size is a control, and starts larger
feat(site): site:dev serves the live bar and reloads it on every rebuild
